title: Khadijah, first believer
hookLine: the angel brings a message for one woman alone: greetings of peace from her Lord (Bukhari)

lines: SHE COMES WITH A VESSEL OF FOOD.
cards: Peace, from her Lord. In a report preserved by Bukhari, the angel Jibril says to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: here is Khadijah, coming to you with a vessel of food.
When she reaches you, give her greetings of peace from her Lord, and from me. A message from heaven, addressed to one person by name, about to arrive with her hands full.
The Qur'an calls the Prophet's wives mothers of the believers. Today, the first of them: Khadijah.

teach.h: HIS WIVES ARE AS THEIR MOTHERS.
teach.b: First, the title of this stretch. Surah thirty-three, verse six, in Pickthall: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers."
So for the next days we meet them one at a time. Why is Khadijah greeted like this? Go back to the night everything began.

teach.h: COVER ME: HE COMES HOME SHAKING.
teach.b: Bukhari's account of the first revelation has the Prophet coming home from the cave of Hira shaking: cover me, cover me. He tells Khadijah he fears for himself.

teach.h: SHE LISTS WHAT SHE HAS SEEN HIM DO.
teach.b: She answers not with a theory but with a list of what she has watched him do. Never, she says. By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you.
You keep the ties of family. You carry the burden of the weak. You give to those who have nothing.
You honor your guest. You stand by people when trouble comes. Then she takes him to her cousin Waraqah, who knew the earlier scriptures, to hear what it might mean.
Tradition remembers her as the first to believe him: by trusting the character she knew, when he himself was afraid.
Aisha says in Bukhari that she never felt jealous of any woman the way she did of Khadijah, though she never saw her, because the Prophet spoke of her so often, and would send gifts to her friends.
In the same report, Jibril adds glad news: a house in Paradise for her, made of hollow pearl, with no noise in it and no weariness.
The one who steadied him in a frightening night is promised a place of quiet.

how: Muslims honor Khadijah among the mothers of the believers, and her words on the night of the first revelation, from Sahih al-Bukhari, are often retold when the beginning of the revelation is taught.

o: the Prophet's first wife, who steadied him
the Prophet's mother, who died when he was small
the Prophet's daughter, who married Ali

p: listed the good he had done
her cousin who knew the earlier books

s: Khadijah calmed him by explaining the angel
she reassured him by listing his good deeds, then took him to Waraqah.

games.q: your husband comes home shaking, saying he fears for himself after something in the cave. what do you do?
o: tell him to keep it secret and rest.
remind him of the good he does, then take him to someone who knows the scriptures.
go to the cave yourself to see what happened.
games.why: in Bukhari she says Allah will never disgrace him, lists his kindness to kin, the weak, the poor and guests, and takes him to Waraqah.

practice: Bring to mind one person who has stayed steady with you, or with someone you love, through a hard stretch.

Do what Khadijah did and make a short list: one thing you have seen them do, then a second, then a third, holding each for a breath. If you pray, ask peace for them by name; if not, simply let the list stand.

wordCard.voice: Khadijah. The Prophet's wife, the one who steadied him on the night of the first revelation, and the one Jibril greeted with peace from her Lord. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: her name, as the hadith of the greeting gives it.

carryVoice: Your line: greeted by her lord. She steadied him with what she had seen. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers.
